title: The host transport reports the claim's named-root binding state at session bind and turn begin, so TermAl learns from Engram when a release has unbound a root it still measures
outcome: The host transport reports the claim's named-root binding state at session bind and turn begin, so TermAl learns from Engram when a release has unbound a root it still measures
acceptance: A release followed by a re-claim of the same claim_id reports unbound_by_release until a new bound event with a fresh generation is recorded; a holder change without a release (handoff accept, recovery by another holder) reports the binding unchanged; tests cover each

The SessionBind and TurnBegin results of the host-private transport carry the bound claim's named-root state as Engram derives it at that cut: none, bound {workspace_id, generation, named_at}, or unbound_by_release {last generation, released at position}; the value is derived from recorded named_root_bind events and the claim's own lifecycle transitions, never from path text or fence inequality
docs/features/behavioral-control-plane.md section 5a documents the field as the authoritative read a host uses to decide when to name again, and TermAl's PI-28 is told the shape

completion.summary: The host transport reports the claim's named-root state (none, bound, unbound_by_release) in session_bind, session_status and turn_begin results, derived from named_root_bind events and the claim's lifecycle; section 5a documents it as the authoritative read; landed as cdb252f and PI-28 told the shape.
